errors.quote: the time must fall below every constant multiple of $n\log n$ along some inputs
errors.problem: The page never says the running time is worst-case, and it states the negation as falling below c n log n 'along some inputs'. Read literally, that is a per-input condition that any machine meets trivially, for example one that handles x=0 in O(n) steps. The paper (lines 381-385) uses the worst-case time T_A(n) and requires liminf_{n->inf} T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0, which means falling below every c n lg n at arbitrarily large input lengths n, worst case over all inputs of that length. The page's later phrase 'not merely along a subsequence' shows a sequence of lengths was meant.

errors.quote: which tends to zero for all large $n$, not merely along a subsequence
errors.problem: A limit does not hold 'for all large n'. The point is that the ratio tends to zero as n -> infinity through all input lengths, which is a limit and not just a liminf. The paper says (line 386) the power saving 'gives a limit of zero through all input lengths, which is a stronger conclusion.'
